clue.text: Indecorous finding due — I will look bad

indicators.note: letters that will look bad are jumbled out of their tidy order, so this signals rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a court finding against them is about to make them look bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorous behaviour lacks propriety and dignity, so it is a near synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Odd end to day tucking into stew of tuna and pilchard? Not half

indicators.note: the day letter tucks itself into the middle of the stew, going inside it
a stew mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged
the pilchard is not taken whole, only its first half is kept
the end of a word is its final letter, so the closing letter of day is taken

explanation.surface: Late in the day someone eats a strange stew of tuna and pilchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untypical is unusual or out of character, which is what odd means.

clue.text: Accomplishing murder? Good

parts.note: to do in is slang for to murder

explanation.surface: A detective's question whether a murder was well done.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a task means carrying it out, so it is a synonym for accomplishing.

clue.text: Beginning to glean from the past description of fifty years?

indicators.note: the first letter of glean

parts.note: olden means of former times

explanation.surface: Gathering memories from long ago to describe half a century.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiftieth anniversary is called a golden one, as in a golden wedding or jubilee.

clue.text: Is welcoming fine conditions

indicators.note: the word is welcomes the fine letter inside it

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone says the weather conditions are fine and welcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs are provisos or stipulations, as in ifs and buts, so they are conditions.

clue.text: Popular volume, impassioned, lacking male participation

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the impassioned word goes without the male letters

parts.note: vehement means forceful and impassioned
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A bestselling passionate book with no men taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: Involvement in an activity is taking part in it, the same as participation.

clue.text: Sailor with two sets of playing-cards?

definitions.text: Sailor with two sets of playing-cards?

parts.words: Sailor with two sets of playing-cards?
parts.note: a deck is a full pack of cards and a hand is the set dealt to one player; joined they name a ship's seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor carrying two packs of cards on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: read the answer as two card-game words, a full pack and a dealt set, that together name a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a seaman who works on the deck of a ship.

clue.text: Consume meal, beginning to end

indicators.note: the first letter of the meal word is shifted to the back

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat a meal right through from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is simply to take it in by mouth, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pop group mostly put out over emcee's opening persuasive speech

indicators.note: in a down clue these letters sit over, above, the next one

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a band

indicators.note: most of the word, the last letter dropped

parts.note: to quench a fire is to put it out

indicators.note: the first letter of emcee's

explanation.surface: A band ejected over its compère's opening speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquence is fluent, forceful skill with words, the quality of a persuasive speech.

clue.text: Flavouring ingredient the writer's upheld in article

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: in a down clue upheld lifts the word, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: the writer refers to themself, so the writer's is my

explanation.surface: A cookery writer has an ingredient upheld in a published article.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb widely used to season food in cooking.

clue.text: Campanologist's permutations? Attempts to keep place

indicators.note: the attempts word holds the place abbreviation within it

parts.note: attempts are tries

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer's sequences, and attempts to secure a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A campanologist is a bell-ringer; Triples is change-ringing on seven bells, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In change-ringing, Triples names the method of permutations rung on seven bells.

clue.text: Coming out on top — very treacherous in winter around hill

indicators.note: the icy word goes around the hill word, enclosing it

parts.note: roads that are icy are treacherous in winter
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Winning the race despite a perilous icy climb around a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming out on top in a contest is winning it, which is what a triumph is.

clue.text: Line taken with arrangement of map tinge regarding colours

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of these words into a new order

explanation.surface: A cartographer adds a line and fiddles with the tints on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to pigments, the substances that give colour.

clue.text: Article on bungled capture is initially aiding recovery

indicators.note: in a down clue the article goes on top of the rest

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: a bungled job is messed up, so the letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of is is used

explanation.surface: A news story about a botched arrest that is helping someone heal.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapeutic treatment is healing, contributing to someone getting better.

clue.text: Optimism with our group taking over power in parliament

indicators.note: the us word takes over the place of the power letter

parts.note: optimism is hope
a group including ourselves is us

explanation.surface: A hopeful political faction seizes control in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative chamber, such as the Commons, is called a House of parliament.

clue.text: Urban area: a US example beginning to mature out of disaster

indicators.note: these letters are taken out of the disaster word

parts.note: a disaster is a calamity
Ala. is the traditional abbreviation for Alabama, one example of a US state

indicators.note: the first letter of mature

explanation.surface: A city described as a US example of an urban area growing out of disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A city is a large town, the classic example of a built-up urban area.

clue.text: Working party's tense attempt to see church

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
you ask for a person when you try to see them
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nervous committee tries to view a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group formed to carry out a specific job, like a working party.

clue.text: Spooner's very, very close at present

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starting sounds here change places

parts.note: very close means near, said aloud the same as a spelling nere
'and how!' is an emphatic way of saying very much so

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner remarks that something is very, very close right now.
explanation.walkthrough: Say NEAR AND HOW and swap the opening sounds N and H: HEAR AND NOW, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at this moment, in the present time, as opposed to past or future.

clue.text: Uncertain quantities supplied by eccentric character in remote region

indicators.note: the character goes in the region word

parts.note: the wilds are remote uninhabited country
a card is an amusing eccentric person

explanation.surface: Unpredictable numbers produced by an oddball living out in the sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild card is an unpredictable element whose effect cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: Italian city criminal stifling expression of surprise

indicators.note: the criminal word smothers the exclamation inside it

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
lor is a dated British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A crook in an Italian city muffles a cry of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan capital, a Renaissance city of Italy.

clue.text: Prominently displayed item's role's tied up with deals

indicators.note: letters tied up in a knot are tangled, so this signals rearranging

explanation.surface: A shop item on display has a part to play in the store's special deals.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss leader is a product sold cheaply and shown off prominently to draw customers in.

clue.text: Protection against water left beside the ocean

indicators.note: the left letter is placed beside the ocean word, after it

parts.note: the ocean is the sea

explanation.surface: Coastal defences left standing beside the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a watertight closure that prevents water leaking through a joint.

clue.text: Collection of information is in French? Really enjoy getting on top of that

indicators.note: in a down clue the enjoy word sits on top of the French word

parts.note: to dig something is slang for really enjoying it
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A query about whether a dossier is in French, and a fan relishing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a compilation or summary of information, such as a law digest.

clue.text: Half-heartedly ran the match, returning to seek postponement

indicators.note: the word is read backwards, as if going back
one of the two central letters, half the heart, is lost

parts.note: a referee who ran the match reffed it

explanation.surface: An official who refereed without enthusiasm then comes back to ask for a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one F from the double-F heart of REFFED, leaving REFED; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to put something off, so seeking postponement amounts to deferring.

clue.text: College splitting in two parts for nobleman

indicators.note: the college letter splits the dual word apart, sitting inside it

parts.note: dual means having two parts

explanation.surface: A college divided in two to accommodate an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to or fit for a duke, a high-ranking nobleman.

clue.text: Former success at bridge all but limiting one bridge team on the outside

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the shortened trick word bounds the other letters, holding them inside
all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: winning a trick is a success at the card game bridge
I is the Roman numeral one
North and South are partners forming one side at bridge

explanation.surface: A former bridge champion keeps one team outside the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means coming from or lying outside, external rather than inherent.

clue.text: Fake source of energy? Disgraceful!

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: the first letter of energy, where it starts

explanation.surface: Outrage at a bogus energy supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame! is an exclamation of condemnation, crying out that something is disgraceful.

clue.text: Item seen on Princess, perhaps, or individual in Court

indicators.note: the or and one words sit inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: an individual is one

explanation.surface: Something worn by a princess or a single person at the royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by royalty such as princesses, or by nobles.

clue.text: Piano recital's first two pieces played alfresco

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, so their order changes

parts.note: the first two letters of recital

explanation.surface: A pianist plays the opening two pieces of a recital outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco, borrowed from Italian, means outdoors, in the fresh air, as with a concert.

clue.text: Eggs on various athletes at the outset

indicators.note: the first letter of each of these words, where each starts

explanation.surface: Athletes eating eggs as fuel before a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural of ovum, the egg cell of a female.

clue.text: Story fellow excluded from biography

indicators.note: the fellow letter is removed from the biography word

parts.note: a biography is a life

explanation.surface: A biographer leaves a particular man out of the life story.
explanation.definitionFit: A story, in the sense of a fib told to deceive, is an untruth.

clue.text: Crafty woman, woman heading off soldier leading other soldiers to ship

indicators.note: the head, first letter, comes off

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a young woman
a soldier ant is a worker ant
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A cunning woman directs a soldier leading his comrades to a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchantress is a sorceress, a woman skilled in magical craft and charm.
